podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Meeting and Kurt Cobain's Death (1994)
podcast.body: The band members, including Shirley Manson, met for the first time in London on April 8, 1994, which tragically coincided with the day Kurt Cobain killed himself. Butch Vig, who had produced Nirvana's "Nevermind," received the news during this initial meeting, causing the project to be temporarily put on hold. "They all met up in London on April 8th of 1994. Yeah, that's that's right. They met for the first time the day Kurt Cobain killed himself."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Plagiarism Charge for "The World Is Not Enough" (1999)
podcast.body: Garbage's theme song for "The World Is Not Enough" faced an "ugly plagiarism charge" from songwriters who claimed it sounded too similar to an unused theme they had written for "The Thomas Crown Affair." Given both films were MGM properties, an internal issue was suspected. The charge was eventually rejected by the courts, allowing the song to remain a solid hit. "There was an ugly plagiarism charge from a couple of songwriters who said this song sounded too much like a theme that they'd written for the Thomas Crown affair but not used."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Russian Border Incident (1999)
podcast.body: In February 1999, while touring Eastern Europe, Garbage attempted to cross the border from Tallinn, Estonia, into Russia for a scheduled show in St. Petersburg. They were denied entry by Russian customs because their road cases were prominently labeled "Garbage." A translator mistakenly interpreted the band's name as a literal declaration of foreign trash, violating a Russian law against its importation. This misunderstanding caused a significant delay and ultimately led to the cancellation of their St. Petersburg performance. "He thought that all these scruffy people were coming to Russia to drop cases and cases of actual garbage on the motherland."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Russian Customs Incident (1999)
podcast.body: On February 4, 1999, Garbage faced problems with Russian customs agents when attempting to cross the border to perform in Tallinn, Estonia. Their road cases were stenciled with the band's name, "Garbage," which Russian customs officials interpreted literally as a declaration of "trash" for export. Despite the band's repeated explanations that it was their name, the agents refused to clear them, leading to the cancellation of their show in Tallinn. "The kids in Tallinn, Estonia did not get their garbage show that night."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 21st Century Reunion
podcast.body: Garbage was included in the list of alt-rock acts that reunited in the first decade of the 21st century, contributing to a period of reformations that brought temporary excitement and engagement back to the scene. "In addition, the Pixies...garbage...These reunions injected some life into the scene, albeit temporary life."

podcast.title: Formation and Search for a Singer
podcast.body: Garbage was formed by producers Butch Vig, Duke Erikson, and sound engineer Steve Marker, who specifically sought a female singer in the vein of Chrissie Hynde or Patty Smith, one who could sing in a lower register. "She was drafted into Garbage by three dudes, butch vig, the record producer, Duke Erickson, and another producer and sound engineer named Steve Marker."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominent Female-Fronted Band
podcast.body: Garbage was noted as part of a generation of interesting bands from the late 90s featuring charismatic female lead singers, with Shirley Manson as their vocalist. "teníamos a Garbage que tenía a Sirly Manson."

srcs.source: Music Radar Clan

podcast.title: Record Deal Secured by Reputation
podcast.body: Garbage sent out samples to record labels with minimal information attached, relying heavily on Butch Vig's established reputation for producing successful albums. This strategy proved effective, as labels agreed to listen and the band ultimately secured a record deal. "Garbage set out samples to record labels with almost no information attached. The only thing anybody knew was that butch vig was involved."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Shirley Manson's "Because the Night" Commentary
podcast.body: Shirley Manson, the lead singer for 90s band Garbage, praised Patti Smith's "Because the Night" for its groundbreaking depiction of female lust. She noted that it was "so unusual" and "thrilling" in the 1970s for a woman to openly express sexual desire, as female sexuality was typically expected to be "covert and hidden" and such themes were usually explored by male artists. "Shirley Manson, who's probably best known for being the lead singer for the 90s man garbage had to say about because the night."

podcast.title: Shirley Manson's Discovery
podcast.body: Steve Marker discovered Shirley Manson singing with a Scottish band called Angel Fish after seeing her on television, leading to her being tracked down for the new project. "But then it was Steve Marker who turned on a TV and saw a Scottish band called Angel Fish and saw Shirley singing for them."

podcast.title: Shirley Manson's Influence
podcast.body: Shirley Manson, the Scottish singer drafted into the American band Garbage, has had a notable impact on contemporary artists. Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evanescence, Katy Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish, and Lana Del Rey. "Her approach to singing and music has been cited as an influence by Amy Lee of Evan Essence, Katie Perry, Lady Gaga, Billie Eilish and Lana Del Rey."

podcast.title: Shirley Manson's Initial Audition Failure
podcast.body: Shirley Manson initially failed her audition for the band. However, due to her shared musical tastes with the other members, they decided to give her another chance, which she then successfully "nailed." "When Shirley finally did have a chance to audition for the band, she failed. But because she had the same taste in music as the guys, they decided to take a chance anyway."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Stage Performance Motivation
podcast.body: Shirley Manson finds stepping on stage to be like a "bolt in the arm," instantly rejuvenating and energizing her. This feeling makes all the "weird things" and difficulties of touring worthwhile, especially when she sees the lit-up faces of the fans enjoying the show. "The minute you step on stage, it's like a bolt in the arm."

xref.title: Chaotic New York Concert (May 15, 1980)
xref.body: Public Image Limited (P.I.L.), led by Johnny Lydon (formerly Johnny Rotten), agreed to play two nights at the Ritz in New York for a $12,000 fee, despite internal squabbles, drug abuse, and money problems. The band was in no shape to play, lacking a drummer (the sixth one quit) and a bass player (who had just walked out). They quickly hired a 65-year-old jazz drummer from a Broadway music shop. Instead of performing live, P.I.L. pantomimed along to their records, hidden from the audience by a large screen with their silhouettes projected by bright white lights. The 1,500 people in the audience were kept waiting in the pouring rain for over an hour, then discovered the band wasn't playing, and Johnny Lydon began taunting and insulting the crowd. This led to a rain of garbage, a storming of the stage, and the destruction of all equipment, with the gig ending after just 25 minutes. "The gig was killed after just 25 minutes."

This tragic event, particularly significant given Vig's role in producing "Nevermind," caused the nascent Garbage project to be put on hold temporarily. "They all met up in London on April 8th of 1994. Yeah, that's that's right. They met for the first time the day Kurt Cobain killed himself."

xref.title: Rejection of Multiple Singers for "The World Is Not Enough" (1999)
xref.body: For "The World Is Not Enough" theme in 1999, David Arnold and the producers considered and rejected a list of prominent artists including Björk, Melanie C of the Spice Girls, Jamiroquai, and Robbie Williams, before ultimately offering the role to Shirley Manson and Garbage. Producers wanted an electronic sound that also retained a big orchestral arrangement. "Calls went out to Bjork, Melanie C of the Spice Girls, Jamira Quye and Robbie Williams and they were all rejected by the producers."

xref.title: Backstage Rider – Specific Catering Demands
xref.body: Catering requirements include dinner for Iggy and two others, available at the venue or a local restaurant, with local cuisine or steak/chicken (or humorously, "endangered species, including moths and anything really cute, snake whale or nurse shark"). It explicitly states that "Cauliflower and broccoli cut into individual florets and then thrown immediately in the garbage." For loadout, two enormous pizzas are requested, often left on the bus to be discarded later due to their unwieldy size. "Cauliflower and broccoli cut into individual florets and then thrown immediately in the garbage."

xref.title: Debunking Kurt Cobain Murder Theory
xref.body: Courtney Love became friends with a host who had previously explored the "Kurt Cobain was murder" conspiracy theory. Through extensive time spent with her, the host concluded that there was "no way" she was involved in any such plot, reinforcing the debunking of the theory as "conspiratorial garbage." "Oddly enough, I became friends with Courtney Love. And I've, has been a lot of time with her and there's no way."

xref.title: Influential Sound
xref.body: My Bloody Valentine, an Irish band, pushed guitar noise and "walls of sound" to new levels, subsequently influencing a vast number of bands. Their sonic approach impacted groups such as The Verve, The Smashing Pumpkins, Nine Inch Nails, Silver Sun Pickups, Garbage, and Nirvana, as well as an uncountable number of shoegaze and fuzz bands. "My Bloody Valentine, an Irish band that took guitar noise and walls of sound to new levels, influencing scores of new bands..."
